messages:
Sam (Product): ok team — sketching a strawman to prioritize the Optimize toolkit work (batching, caching, quant recommendations, eval-triggered alerts). want quick alignment before i turn into a formal PRD.
Jordan (Eng): 👍 send the tradeoffs you care about. perf vs cost vs ops complexity?
Sam (Product): exactly. proposed priority order: 1) lightweight batching heuristics + API flags (low risk, high immediate cost wins) 2) prefix/KV caching primitives + SDK hooks (medium risk) 3) quant recommendation engine (ML + infra coordination) 4) eval-triggered alerts (higher product/ops integration). rationale: customers repeatedly ask for easier batching first.
Priya (ML): quick notes — quant recs need scope: are we recommending per-model quant levels or per-route profiles? per-route lets us optimize for lat/quality per workload, but needs route metadata + eval hooks.
Marta (CS): from pilots: customers want "safe" quant suggestions (e.g., down to 4-bit only on synthetic eval pass). they also want a rollback path and obvious visible quality monitors.
Jordan (Eng): infra constraints: implementing continuous batching heuristics is small (2-3 sprint-ish). caching primitives are trickier because KV lifetime management + cache invalidation across model variants is hairy.
Alex (DevEx): SDK/API standpoint — recommend exposing two things: a) per-request hints ("batch_preference": "low|auto|high") and b) route-level policy config. sample snippet:```json
{
  "route": "/generate",
  "batch_preference": "auto",
  "cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl_s": 300 }
}
```
Sam (Product): love that. for launch criteria i propose:
- batching: measurable >=15% token-cost reduction on typical PLG demo apps without >50ms median tail increase
- caching: clear API + SDK with cache invalidation story + at least 2 pilot customers using it
- quant recs: quant profiles + canary rollout support + documented expected quality delta per profile
- eval-alerts: can trigger manual triage + alert dedupe + one pilot integration with SRE/CS
Jordan (Eng): can we add an engineering gating checklist: perf tests pass, smoke tests for tail, rollout rollback tested, and a config migration script?
Sam (Product): yes. add to PRD.
Priya (ML): for quant recs acceptance: need an automated eval job that runs candidate quant profiles against a baseline prompt set and surface metrics: accuracy, hallucination rate, perplexity-ish proxy. also a confidence band when recommending.
Marta (CS): customers want the eval-triggered alerts tied to human-readable examples. when an alert fires, the ticket should include: failing prompts, baseline vs current outputs, and suggested action (e.g., rollback to fp16, increase temperature, or pin model).
Jordan (Eng): ops-bot: created checklist ticket #OPT-942 for batching perf tests :thumbsup:
ops-bot: ticket OPT-942 created by @Jordan.
Alex (DevEx): docs/workflow: need a migration guide for customers who have custom batching on their side. also add code samples for cache usage and example alert payloads.
Sam (Product): decision time: do we run this as a single "Optimize Toolkit" launch or phase into "Batching & Cache v1" then quant+alerts in v2? my recommendation: phased — get batching+simple cache out quickly (v1), then follow with quant recs (v2), then eval-alerts (v3). reduces cross-team coupling and gives customers fast wins.
Priya (ML): agree — v1 yield immediate cost wins; v2 needs more ML infra work.
Marta (CS): phased is easier for customer adoption. v1 can be in the docs as "Beta: batching & cache" and we ask selected pilots.
Jordan (Eng): timeline sketch: v1 (batching + basic cache SDK) — 6 weeks; v2 (quant recs engine + rollout tooling) — 10 weeks after v1; v3 (eval-alerter + integrations) — 6 weeks post v2. these are rough.
Sam (Product): action items: @Jordan draft eng gating checklist and rough sprint plan; @Priya define eval metrics and baseline prompt sets; @Alex draft SDK API + examples; @Marta identify 2 pilot customers and craft onboarding flow. i'll consolidate into PRD Monday.
Marta (CS): i'll ping AcmeCorp + NovaApps today for pilot interest.
Jordan (Eng): noted. starting a branch for batching heuristics.
Alex (DevEx): i'll stub docs and sample configs.
Sam (Product): thanks all — this is enough to move forward. leaving this thread open for quick follow-ups. :rocket:
